# gpupaas_kubernetes_cluster_kubeconfig (Data Source)

The user kubeconfig of a running first-class managed Kubernetes cluster, the same file the console's "Download Kubeconfig" gives. It is read each time Terraform refreshes, so it follows the credentials the platform issues. The cluster must be registered and running, or the read fails. The platform issues new client credentials with every download, so the value differs between reads: Terraform shows it as a changed output, never as a resource change. The platform looks the cluster up by name only, so the read fails if the name matches more than one cluster (for example in two projects) rather than return another cluster's credentials. The kubeconfig is sensitive and is stored in the state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The kubeconfig of a running cluster, as the console's "Download Kubeconfig" gives it.
data "gpupaas_kubernetes_cluster_kubeconfig" "k" {
  name      = "demo-cluster"
  project   = "system-catalog"
  workspace = "team-a"
}

# It is sensitive. Write it to a file only where that is acceptable.
resource "local_sensitive_file" "kubeconfig" {
  content         = data.gpupaas_kubernetes_cluster_kubeconfig.k.kubeconfig
  filename        = "${path.module}/kubeconfig.yaml"
  file_permission = "0600"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the cluster.
- `project` (String)

### Optional

- `workspace` (String) Workspace that owns the cluster; omit for a project-scoped cluster.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `kubeconfig` (String, Sensitive) The kubeconfig file content (YAML).
